decisions.reason: The zero-word-space exclusion was unqualified, whereas maximality bounds only constituents of M. The exact corner and maximal-tail reconstruction prove one contributing orbit among those constituents. Qualified both clauses to M, retaining the factorial multiplicity, cross-field label detection and virtual-character injectivity. BK section 4.12 Lemma 4.21 states the module-relative multiplicity formula, not a global word separation theorem; arbitrary fields are covered by the local maximal-tail and crystal suppliers.

Step 6.1 asserts the transported Fock removal formula and the same formula for its projection, not an unshifted Specht restriction identity. The canonical action supplier explicitly gives E_can|alpha=q^(-1-h_i(alpha))E_basic. For e=2, mu=(1,1), i=1, h_i(alpha)=0, d_A=0 and d^A=1, so canonical Specht restriction is q^(-1)[S(1)], exactly the projected Fock formula. The actual consumer proves equality on projective-word evaluations using contravariance and h_i+1-d^A=d_A. Independently checked the unitriangular minor, H(0)=I, inverse-Gram projection and upper-dual expansion; no defect requires editing.

The Definition and steps 1.1–1.4 correctly construct the generic groups and transport only H^Lambda to R^Lambda. The extra assertion in step 2.1 identified an arbitrary tower R with R^Lambda without a hypothesis; the tower having only R_0=k gives Laurent rank one, unlike the level-one cyclotomic tower. Replaced that assertion with the H^Lambda-to-R^Lambda identification already proved. This is nonfatal to the defined interface because no Definition clause or necessary construction relied on the extra assertion.

At the vacuum block, P=k direct-sum k{1} has degree support {0,1}, so P{r} has support {r,r+1} and its Hom dual has support {-r,-r-1}; equality would require 2r=-1. Thus F3 and step 1.4 overstate normalization. The actual duality and quotient-cover suppliers normalize simple orbits and their indecomposable covers only. Restricted F3 and step 1.4 to those objects. The Hom-pairing Definition, finite Laurent values, additive descent and q^(s-r) shift rule were already valid and remain unchanged; the extra overstatement is nonfatal to that interface.

The blockwise BK Statement requires nonzero e_alpha, so it alone cannot identify C_F with H_alpha(F) in the zero-sector case needed for each dimension inequality. Added the existing early all-sector isomorphism as a direct dependency and F2 citation. It identifies the integer KLR presentation over F with the Hecke sector even when zero; the presentation then surjects onto F tensor L, forcing that tensor to vanish when the sector does. Freeness and the characteristic-zero base change give each rank inequality; the fixed total Hecke dimension forces equality content by content and supplies the inverse generator-matching map. No assumption of support preservation and no weakened Definition are used. Read BK section 6 Theorems 6.1 and 6.4 and their complete proofs, as well as the local all-sector proof.

F4 calls the same-row relation r to_T s a weak Bruhat arrow, contradicting the supplier Definition, which distinguishes it from T xrightarrow{r} S with S=s_rT and both tableaux standard. Replaced the misdescription with the exact same-row, strictly-right relation and the graph-edge distinction. The brick proofs use only the same-row meaning already in the Statement: terminal consecutive entries occupy a rightmost row segment. Verified the signed corner count, double-neighbor e=2 Cartan update, defect recursion, degree-plus-codegree induction, and cancellation of above-row corners across a full residue brick. No Statement change or proof inference depended on a Bruhat edge, so this is nonfatal.
